chunks: Ahmad b. Yahya al-Mukattib narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Qasim narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Sa'id al-Dimashqi narrated to us. He said: Al-Zubayr b. Bakkar narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Dahhak narrated to us from Nawfal b. 'Amira. He said: Qusay b. Kilab advised his sons and then said:
"O my sons! Beware of drinking wine, for even if it rectifies the bodies, it corrupts the minds."

key_terms.الأبدان: the bodies - Physical bodies, contrasted with minds
key_terms.الأذهان: the minds - Intellects and reasoning faculties
key_terms.الخمر: wine/alcohol - All intoxicating beverages, later prohibited in Quran 5:90-91

ai.seo_question: What did Qusay ibn Kilab say about drinking wine?
ai.summary: This narration preserves pre-Islamic Arab wisdom from Qusay ibn Kilab, an ancestor of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) and custodian of the Ka'ba, who advised his sons against alcohol. His argument was pragmatic: even granting wine's supposed physical benefits, the damage to mental faculties is far worse. The saying was preserved in Islamic tradition to show that wise Arabs recognized the harm of intoxicants before the Quranic prohibition.
